extracted.intended_audience: Army public affairs officers, commanders, and personnel responsible for public communications, speaker engagement, and use/clearance of military assets
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for Army public affairs: rules for release of information, speaker and manuscript clearance, use of military assets (bands, ceremonial units, exhibits), and procedures for coordination with higher headquarters and civilian media/organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to Military Entrance Processing Stations
rubrics_metrics.description: See Joint service regulation AR 601–270, paragraph 3–12 for guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for media access to MEPS must follow the joint-service regulation referenced; coordinate per that guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to commissaries
rubrics_metrics.description: All requests received from news media representatives to visit commissary facilities will be coordinated with the PA office of the Defense Commissary Agency, Fort Lee, VA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media requests are not handled locally without coordination; forward requests to the specified PA office for approval and coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visits to installations with chemical/nuclear/biological defense activities
rubrics_metrics.description: All news media requests to cover NBC missions or activities will be considered on a case-by-case basis and should normally be approved by the chemical activity or installation commander when such visits will not interfere with operational requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval may be denied for safety or security reasons; weigh operational impact, safety, and security in deciding access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to Army confinement facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: News media access to and photography in an Army confinement facility normally is prohibited (see AR 190–47, paragraph 10–12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat confinement facilities as normally off-limits to media; consult referenced regulation for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information on ongoing criminal investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, no information should be released concerning ongoing investigations without close coordination with local authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs may acknowledge the existence of an investigation after coordination. Any released information must not violate the Privacy Act or impede an ongoing criminal investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspector General (IG) records and release authority
rubrics_metrics.description: IG records are privileged documents... The designated release authority for all IG records is The Inspector General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use or release IG records without authorization; unauthorized release can breach confidentiality and compromise IG effectiveness. See AR 20–1, chap 3 for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army support to disaster relief — prompt information release
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on Army participation in disaster relief operations will be made available promptly to news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARNG and USAR PAOs should forward news/feature material to OCPA for possible national dissemination; upon conclusion provide OCPA a narrative summary of PA activities and results; provide info copies to intermediate HQs.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCPA responsibility for civil disturbances
rubrics_metrics.description: The OCPA is responsible for PA activities in connection with civil disturbances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer public information questions on civil disturbances to OCPA for AA elements and RC units on active Federal duty; ARNG units on state active duty refer to NGB PA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of information by contractors and other non-Army entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Army review and clearance of materials proposed for release to the public by contractors, manufacturers, researchers, and other entities regarding contractual agreements, awards, products, services, military sales, technology, scientific studies, and other related areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy favors releasing maximum accurate information but excepts safeguarded information, nonexportable commercial data/ITAR-controlled info, and material on the Militarily Critical Technologies List. PAOs should clear releases at the lowest level possible; where higher HQ release is required, forward material and recommendation to OCPA. PAOs must not release material implying DA endorsement, comparative merit claims, DOD spec details or acceptance-test results, or critical military technology. Procedures at appendix F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of information on unit deployments
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD provides the initial public release for deployments of units at the brigade combat team level and above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unit PAOs must attempt to notify families prior to initial announcement. Units below BCT not announced by DOD/OCPA may make public announcement only after receipt of deployment orders and family notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory clearance for official speeches/manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearance, through security review and PA channels, is required for all official speeches and writings that are presented or published in the civilian domain, to include materials placed on the Internet or released via similar electronic media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual speech writers/authors/speakers are responsible for ensuring content review and clearance prior to public release; maximize use of email in the clearance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for speakers — referral to PAO
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations wanting to invite an Army speaker are referred to the PAO of the nearest installation likely to have a subject matter expert; if local spokespersons unavailable, refer to OCPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local PAO as primary point of contact to identify appropriate Army speakers and coordinate requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding and travel for official speaking engagements
rubrics_metrics.description: Official public speaking is considered mission related and may be charged to normal mission travel and per diem accounts; accepting a gratuity or fee is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsoring organizations may reimburse necessary travel/lodging in lieu of Government reimbursement per Joint Travel Regulations. Distant travel may be authorized for specified patriotic observances, significant ceremonies, or when audience/occasion justify presence; educational forum participation is encouraged for military education institution personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential platform speaker selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of the Army is sometimes required to furnish an officer to represent the President... A general officer will be designated unless overriding reasons preclude it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate a general officer by default for Presidential platform representation unless specific reasons dictate otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medal of Honor recipient appearance policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders will give special attention to public appearances by MOH recipients... balance public recognition with protection from exploitation and overexposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider personal preferences and event value equally; discourage school appearances that interfere with training/education; obtain proper clearances if absence from duty is necessary; sponsors are responsible for transportation/food/lodging costs; local commanders may approve appearances outside local area; maintain and forward updated biographical data and photos to OCPA upon transfer or rank change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearance authorities and prepublication review
rubrics_metrics.description: HQDA and/or OSD clearance is required for all speeches, manuscripts, or communications products containing information meeting criteria in paragraph 5–3. Items mentioning names of military personnel, military operations, or subjects listed in para 5‑3a(1)–(20) must be submitted for prepublication review through Army PA channels (see DODD 5230.09).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit material prior to release to any non-DoD persons (including ghostwriters, agents, editors, publishers). Unofficial materials not addressing military matters per para 5‑3a do not require clearance, but authors must ensure security is not compromised; open-source information does not constitute declassification and aggregation may create classified information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official speaking/writing scope and expertise requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Speeches or remarks must address a subject within a speaker’s official expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members may speak on unrelated matters when consistent with other laws/regulations, not conflicting with duties, and not implying Government endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official materials review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Official speech text and written materials must be reviewed through PA channels and cleared for security, accuracy, policy, and propriety by proper authority, at the lowest level possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs with subject matter expertise and audience knowledge should review/clear locally where possible; if not possible, escalate to next appropriate level. The process is a safeguard (not censorship) to prevent accidental release of classified/inaccurate/inappropriate information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred format for review
rubrics_metrics.description: For review and clearance purpose, full-text format speeches are preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speech outlines, slides without text, or bullet-format presentations may be reviewed/cleared to keep PAOs informed and facilitate unofficial advice, but full text is preferred. Abstracts or notes are not substitutes; abstracts to be published in advance require clearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions on official endorsement and partisan activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Official speeches/writings must not contradict U.S. Government policy or law and must adhere to DOD 5500.7–R. Army employees will not officially endorse, or appear to endorse, membership drives or fund-raisers for any non-Federal entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heads of ACOM/organizations may authorize employees to express Army policy as speakers. Review AR 600–20 and consult legal office when participation in partisan political gatherings is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding staged controversy and consultation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations where an event’s real or apparent purpose is to stage controversy and/or confrontation will be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult OCPA before providing speakers for events where public confrontation or debate of national policy is planned or likely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on endorsing private individuals or groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Material must not endorse, promote, or sponsor any private individual, group, or venture or give the appearance of doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events supported should be of common public interest and benefit; participation authorized only if accommodations available without regard to protected characteristics; special rules apply where organizations' qualifications are gender or national origin based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance distribution and revalidation of cleared material
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance distribution of copies of cleared material may be arranged and is encouraged to gain widest dissemination. Prior to repetitively using a previously cleared speech or manuscript, the clearance should be revalidated by the approving PAO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate distribution with host organizations and revalidate clearances for repeat use to ensure content remains appropriate and accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unofficial writing and academic exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Unofficial materials not dealing with the military per paragraph 5‑3a do not require clearance; students and faculty are not required to submit academic papers prepared for academic requirements when not intended for release outside the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If intended for public release or placed in public-access libraries, submit for review. Clearance will be granted if classified information is not disclosed, DOD interests not jeopardized, and the author accurately portrays official policy even if critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of DOD identification in unofficial writings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual who uses a title or other identification connected with DOD in an unofficial writing or speech will include a disclaimer that views are the author's and do not reflect official policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requested by reviewing authority, the writer must not use DOD titles/identifiers. Comply with ethics rules when accepting payment for unofficial work (5 CFR 2635.807, DOD 5500.7‑R).

rubrics_metrics.name: Security review requirement for retirees and former employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Retired personnel, former DOD employees, and nonactive duty members of the RCs will use the DOD security review process to ensure that information they submit for public release does not compromise national security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow prepublication/pre-release security review processes when material meets review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local clearance procedures and submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs will establish local clearance procedures. Most clearances will be completed at local level. Materials requiring HQDA or OSD clearance will be submitted to the OCPA with full/final text and supplemental visuals, in triplicate, in sufficient time for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denials or mandatory changes may be appealed through original submission channels to OCPA. Manuscripts lacking proper clearance sent to official Army publications will be forwarded by editors to proper clearance authority. Joint/unified command-originating material cleared per those commands' procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of military musical, aerial, ceremonial, and troop units for public events
rubrics_metrics.description: Army commanders are encouraged to provide marching units, bands, color guards, drill teams, aerial demonstrations, static displays, exhibits, and similar support for public-domain functions to maximize public events supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests requiring DOD/DA approval are forwarded through channels to OCPA; ARNG requests to HQDA (NGB PA); use prescribed DD Forms 2535/2536 for requests requiring DoD/DA approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized participation conditions for musical/ceremonial support
rubrics_metrics.description: Army musical, ceremonial, and troop support is authorized for official military functions, official civil ceremonies, civilian-sponsored public events intended to stimulate interest/support recruiting or patriotism, civilian social/cultural events if patriotic music is performed, traditional military events for morale/families, and certain sports events under conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sports participation limited to specified circumstances (scheduled regular season events, amateur regular season events where participation incidental and in Army's best interest, pregame activities when not nationally televised and confined to honoring colors). Activities in malls/shopping centers to support recruiting require musicians in uniform, must not be presented as promotions for the venue, must primarily attract visitors to recruiting displays, and must not reflect unfavorably on the Army.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited participation by Army musicians
rubrics_metrics.description: Army musicians on official duty are prohibited from providing background, dinner, or dance music at events funded solely by NAFs (with limited exceptions); prohibited from receiving remuneration that competes with local civilian musicians; generally may not receive pay for official performance in support of public events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions exist for events sponsored by certain military welfare societies per statute and guidance. Off‑duty paid performances allowed unless verified complaints of competition with civilians. Army participation/support not authorized for motion picture premieres, commercially sponsored parades, beauty contests/pageants, etc. Duration normally not exceed 3 days per event; comply with 10 USC 974, DOD 5500.7‑R, and AR 220‑90 for weather policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Band tour procedures and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: CONUS band travel outside normal community relations area must coordinate through channels with OCPA; concert tours (more than 3 nights away) require prior OCPA approval; OCONUS tours have duration limits (not to exceed 15 days without OASD(PA) approval, single locations not exceed 7 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tour areas assigned by OASD(PA) and coordinated among services; tours outside assigned area require approval. Ensure requests routed to appropriate authorities and meet timing/approval requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical support content and event limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Musical support of non‑Federal event sponsors is limited to patriotic, military, and other selections that demonstrate professionalism and focus on Army music presentation; dinner/background/dance music is not authorized at civilian-sponsored events unless sponsor is specified military welfare society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No event to receive support of more than one band without OASD(PA) approval. Background/dinner/social music is authorized for official USG events supported by appropriated funds. Memorial service support limited to those authorized for state funeral or military honors or approved by OASD(PA). Military musicians may perform nontraditional music at professional development conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCONUS performance approvals and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: United States‑based Army musical units may perform OCONUS only with prior approval of OASD(PA), the appropriate OCONUS commander, and the host nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCONUS support requests must be forwarded by sponsor to unified combatant commander or OASD(PA); unified command must determine adequate in‑theater assets are unavailable and event justifies CONUS assets; OASD(PA) evaluates and forwards approvals to the appropriate Service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for ceremonial units and volunteers
rubrics_metrics.description: Ceremonial units include color guards, drill teams, and specialized units appropriate for military and patriotic ceremonies; locally authorized volunteer units should be well‑trained, have professional bearing, and operate at no additional cost to the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure volunteer units meet training and cost requirements before authorizing local participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Armed Forces Color Guard composition and flag policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A Joint Armed Forces Color Guard composition is prescribed (two Army flag bearers with national and Army colors; one each Marine, Navy, Air Force, Coast Guard colors; one Army and one Marine rifleman escorts). When a Joint guard cannot be formed, senior service member carries national colors; Soldiers carry colors when present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Army personnel may carry foreign nation flags only when an official of that nation is present in an official capacity for whom honors normally would be rendered; otherwise Army personnel in uniform are not authorized to carry flags of foreign nations or nonmilitary organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibits: purpose, approvals, and display rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Army exhibits (mission exhibits, models, devices, information materials) primarily support recruiting/retention or further Army professional, scientific, and technical interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OASD(PA) must approve PA exhibits at national and international events; requests forwarded via DD Form 2536 at least 45 days in advance. Local commanders may approve local event participation. Exhibits may be displayed in public commercial spaces if not used specifically to draw the public to the location or used in advertising/promotional activities; the requesting agency is responsible for indemnification/shipping for loans (see AR 870–5).
